_note: Primary sources shown from the History event cards. Images from Wikimedia Commons (licence and author per item). Quotes are short excerpts of standard English translations (Grayson/Glassner for the chronicles, Finkel for the Cyrus Cylinder, Oppenheim in ANET for the Nabonidus Cylinder and the Jehoiachin tablets).

chron605.name: Babylonian Chronicle (ABC 5, the ‘Jerusalem Chronicle’)
chron605.quote: “He crossed the river to encounter the army of Egypt which was encamped at Carchemish … The army of Egypt retreated before him.” … “On the first day of the month Elul he ascended the royal throne in Babylon.”
chron605.note: A Babylonian scribe’s year-by-year record. It dates Nebuchadnezzar’s victory at Carchemish and his accession to 605 BC, and later his capture of ‘the city of Judah’ in 597 BC (cf. Daniel 1:1–2; 2 Kings 24).

jehoiachin.name: Jehoiachin’s ration tablet
jehoiachin.quote: “… for Ya’ukinu, king of the land of Yahudu …”
jehoiachin.note: Ration lists excavated in Nebuchadnezzar’s palace at Babylon name Jehoiachin, the exiled king of Judah, and his sons, matching 2 Kings 25:27–30.

brick.name: Stamped brick of Nebuchadnezzar II
brick.quote: “Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, provider for Esagila and Ezida, eldest son of Nabopolassar, king of Babylon.”
brick.note: Bricks across the city carry his name. Excavations from 1899 to 1917 uncovered his palaces, walls and the Ishtar Gate, the building work behind his boast in Daniel 4:30.
brick.credit: Photo: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin, CC BY-SA 4.0

nabcyl.name: Nabonidus Cylinder from Ur
nabcyl.quote: “… and as for Belshazzar, the eldest son, my offspring, instill reverence for your great godhead in his heart …”
nabcyl.note: Before these cylinders were read, Belshazzar was known only from Daniel and some critics doubted he existed. They name him as Nabonidus’s eldest son.

nabchron.name: Nabonidus Chronicle
nabchron.quote: “The king was in Tema; the prince, his officers and his army were in Akkad.” … “On the sixteenth day, Ugbaru, governor of the Guti, and the army of Cyrus entered Babylon without battle.”
nabchron.note: It shows Nabonidus away for years while ‘the prince’ ruled in Babylon, which is why Belshazzar could offer Daniel only the third place in the kingdom (Daniel 5:16, 29). It dates the fall of Babylon to October 539 BC.

cyrus.name: Cyrus Cylinder
cyrus.quote: “I am Cyrus, king of the universe, the great king, the powerful king, king of Babylon, king of Sumer and Akkad, king of the four quarters of the world.”
cyrus.note: Royal propaganda from 539 BC. It also says Cyrus returned deported peoples and their gods to their homes, consistent with the decree in Ezra 1.

mosaic.name: The Alexander Mosaic (Battle of Issus)
mosaic.quote: Alexander charges on Bucephalus as Darius III turns his chariot to flee.
mosaic.note: A Roman floor mosaic from Pompeii (c. 100 BC), probably after a Greek painting made within a generation of the battle. Daniel 8:7: “there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand.”

titus.name: Arch of Titus: the spoils of Jerusalem
titus.quote: “SENATVS POPVLVSQVE ROMANVS DIVO TITO DIVI VESPASIANI F VESPASIANO AVGVSTO.” (The Senate and People of Rome, to the deified Titus Vespasian Augustus, son of the deified Vespasian.)
titus.note: Built after AD 81, its relief shows soldiers carrying the Temple’s menorah in triumph, the destruction foretold in Daniel 9:26.
